1	# Emerging Market Debt Vulnerability & Fed Rate Transmission (2021–2024)
2	
3	## Overview
4	Four datasets capture the transmission of US monetary tightening to eight emerging-market economies (Turkey, Argentina, Egypt, South Africa, Brazil, Pakistan, Ghana, Sri Lanka) across four dimensions: US interest rates, external debt burdens, currency depreciation, and sovereign credit rating actions.
5	
6	## Data Source
7	
8	### fed_funds_rate
9	Quarterly upper-bound Fed Funds rate from Q4 2021 to Q4 2024. Fields: `date` (YYYY-QN string), `rate_pct` (float, percent). 13 rows.
10	
11	### external_debt_to_gdp
12	Annual external-debt-to-GDP ratios for 8 countries, 2021–2024. Fields: `country` (string), `year` (int), `debt_gdp_pct` (float, percent of GDP). 32 rows.
13	
14	### currency_depreciation
15	Cumulative local-currency depreciation against the USD from a January 2021 baseline, measured at year-end. Fields: `country` (string), `year` (int), `depreciation_pct` (float, positive = weaker). 32 rows.

01 — Fed Rate Trajectory & EM Currency Depreciation

US Federal Funds Rate

Quarter-end upper-bound rate, Q4 2021 – Q4 2024. The steepest tightening phase (2022–Q2 to 2023–Q3) coincides with the largest EM stress events.

Tightening phase: 525 bps hike from Q4 2021 → Q3 2023. Rate held at 5.50% for four consecutive quarters before first cut in Q3 2024.

Cumulative Currency Depreciation vs USD

From January 2021 baseline to year-end. Higher values = weaker local currency. Argentina and Turkey bear the most stress; Brazil remained most resilient.

02 — Vulnerability Spectrum: External Debt vs Currency Depreciation (2024)

External Debt-to-GDP vs Cumulative Depreciation (2024 snapshot)

Each bubble represents a country. X-axis: external debt as % of GDP (2024). Y-axis: cumulative currency depreciation from Jan 2021. Bubble size scales with debt-to-GDP. Countries in the upper-right quadrant face compounded vulnerability.

Upper-right quadrant (high debt + high depreciation): Argentina (72.1% / 85.6%) and Turkey (56.4% / 73.2%) face the greatest compounded external vulnerability. Ghana (63.7%) and Sri Lanka (68.2%) carry high debt burdens but default has partially unwound currency pressure.

03 — External Debt Trajectories 2021–2024

External Debt as % of GDP — Annual Snapshots

Argentina, Ghana, and Sri Lanka show the steepest debt accumulation during the hiking cycle. Brazil stands apart as the only country with stable-to-declining external debt ratios.

04 — Sovereign Rating Actions vs Fed Rate Phases

Credit Rating Timeline: Downgrades Cluster in 2022–2023

Rating actions mapped against the tightening cycle. Red = downgrade, blue = upgrade, green = affirmed, dark red = selective default. The 2022 tightening phase triggered the most concentrated downgrade activity across all 8 countries.

Downgrade Upgrade Affirmed Default
Downgrade clustering: 9 of 12 recorded downgrades occurred between Feb 2022 and Oct 2023 — perfectly aligned with the Fed's steepest tightening phase (+525 bps). Ghana and Sri Lanka entered selective default within 7 months of each other.

05 — Debt Burden vs Depreciation Magnitude (Comparative)

External Debt/GDP (2024)

Countries ranked by 2024 external debt burden. Argentina and Sri Lanka exceed 68% of GDP.

Cumulative Currency Depreciation (2024)

Countries ranked by depreciation from Jan 2021 baseline. High-debt EMs tend to show greater depreciation — Argentina most stark.

Debt–depreciation link: Countries with external debt above 50% of GDP (Argentina, Sri Lanka, Ghana, Turkey) uniformly experienced cumulative depreciation above 40%, while lower-debt economies (Brazil, South Africa) stayed under 25%. This underscores the amplifying role of external debt exposure during dollar-tightening cycles.

Sources: Federal Reserve (FRED), IMF World Economic Outlook, S&P / Moody's / Fitch composite ratings (simplified). Currency data from Jan 2021 baseline to year-end. External debt figures estimated, rounded to 1 decimal place. Sri Lanka and Ghana entered selective default during observation period. Analysis period: Q4 2021 – Q4 2024.
